name: known-gap-depth-blind-scoring
reason: Every required skill here is matched by a NOVICE skill with 1-2 years: React (1.5), TypeScript (2.0), DynamoDB (1.0), WebSockets (1.5). ScoreTechnicalFit returns a perfect 100 -- identical to the score it gives a JD requiring Go, PostgreSQL, and Kafka, where the persona is expert with 9-11 years. The scorer cannot tell the difference because it never sees the difference: ListActiveSkillTagNamesByUser (internal/db/queries/skills.sql) selects t.name only, so proficiency and years_experience are dropped at the query layer before scoring begins. ListActiveSkillsByUser already returns the full rows. This is the mechanism behind #44's 'your profile covers Python, Kubernetes, and cloud-native work' narrative. The band below is what a depth-aware scorer should produce for an all-novice match; it is not a claim about the exact weighting, which is a design decision.
description: Synthetic signals, not drawn from a JD fixture. Isolates depth from every other variable: four required skills, all matched, all shallow.

screening_summary.industry: synthetic fixture, not a real posting

technical_score.comment: Full coverage at novice depth must not score like full coverage at expert depth.

technical_gaps.comment: Coverage is genuinely complete -- the defect is the weighting, not the matching.
